summary:
Developed by Farida El Atroush, Mohamed Nasser, Rawan Mohya, Mariam Ahmed, and Heba El Hares, this project is a comprehensive educational infographic guide detailing the historical missions, successes, partial failures, and complete failures of lunar and Martian rovers and spacecraft (such as those from NASA, CNSA, USSR, ISRO, and JAXA).
Addressing the Challenge
The project investigates why space missions fail by analyzing five repeating core problems: dust accumulation on solar panels, mechanical failures/stuck wheels, extreme cold/long nights, landing errors, and aerial/navigation risks. It directly addresses these challenges by proposing specific engineering solutions for future missions, such as implementing nuclear power (RTG) to maintain heat and energy during dust storms, utilizing self-cleaning solar panels and dust-proof radiator covers, building stronger mobility systems (like larger wheels and backup motors), and incorporating smart 3D landing sensors and automated orientation recovery.
Importance
This work is vital because it turns historical challenges into learning opportunities. By diagnosing past mission setbacks, it provides a crucial engineering roadmap and operational framework to ensure greater reliability and success for future space exploration on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
details:
The project is a comprehensive educational guide and infographic suite detailing the historical missions, landing dates, successes, partial failures, and complete failures of lunar and Martian rovers and spacecraft (such as missions by NASA, CNSA, USSR, ISRO, and JAXA). It works by breaking down historical mission timelines and mapping out repeating failure patterns—such as dust storms, stuck wheels, and freezing nights—to systematically connect them with specific engineering solutions.
Benefits and intended impact: The project provides an invaluable educational framework and engineering roadmap for future space missions. Its intended impact is to turn past mission setbacks into lessons, guiding future aerospace designs to achieve higher reliability and success when exploring the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
Tools, languages, hardware, and software: The project integrates extensive multi-agency data (from NASA, CNSA, ISRO, ROSCOSMOS, and JAXA) into structured, beautifully organized educational infographics and visual layouts designed for space exploration learning.
Creativity of the project: The project creatively bridges historical data and future engineering by transforming complex space mission statistics into clear, accessible visual comparisons. It uses structured color-coded legends (green for success, yellow for partial failure, blue for ongoing/still working) and side-by-side problem-and-solution breakdowns to make aerospace engineering engaging and easy to understand.
Considered factors: Your team considered the root causes behind why past rovers stopped working—specifically focusing on five major hurdles: dust on solar panels, stuck wheels/mechanical failures, extreme cold during long nights, landing errors, and aerial/navigation risks. You also factored in multi-agency collaboration by incorporating international missions from various countries to present a complete global perspective on space exploration.
